# New hypothesis: remove all green blocks, then move RIGHT to trigger screen change, repeat
# Let me try removing all 7 green blocks first, then moving RIGHT

# Get green block positions
seg = current_frame.segmentation

# Click centers of all 7 green blocks

for g in greens:
    gc = [p[1] for p in g['boundary']]

    seg = current_frame.segmentation
    remaining = len([n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N'])
    done = result.get('level_completed') or result.get('done')
    print(f"Click ({click['row']},{click['col']}): greens={remaining}, done={done}")
    if done:
        print("LEVEL COMPLETED!")
        break

# After removing all greens, move RIGHT to trigger screen change
if not done:
    seg = current_frame.segmentation
    greens_after = len([n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N'])
    print(f"\nAfter removing all: {greens_after} greens remaining")
    
    # Move RIGHT multiple times to trigger screen change
    for i in range(5):
        result = action(['RIGHT'])
        seg = current_frame.segmentation
        player = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'b'][0]
        pc = [p[1] for p in player['boundary']]
        greens_now = len([n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N'])
        done = result.get('level_completed') or result.get('done')
        print(f"RIGHT #{i+1}: player cols {min(pc)}-{max(pc)}, greens={greens_now}, done={done}")
        if done:
            print("LEVEL COMPLETED!")
            break
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
